prompt_en: A tense espionage photograph centered on a reference-guided woman, a moment of clandestine human contact at a covered railway-station flower stall on a rainy morning. Use the supplied reference image for her soft oval facial proportions and dark eyes, and her short black bob with a wispy parted fringe. She is choosing a paper-wrapped bunch of white chrysanthemums in a charcoal wool coat; her restrained, alert presence and the pale window light across her cheek give her a quiet personal magnetism. A man in an ordinary brown commuter jacket stands immediately to her left, screen right, their shoulders angled slightly away from one another. One person extends an envelope while the other person's open hand remains separated from it by a visible gap. The man is the giver: his right thumb and fingers hold the far short edge of a small sealed cream envelope at waist height, extended toward her. Her empty left palm is turned upward beside her coat pocket, with a clear strip of background visible between her nearest fingertip and the envelope's near edge. The envelope and her receiving hand remain parallel and separate in the open gap between their bodies. Both wrists and the forearms connecting these hands to their respective bodies are visible. Her right hand supports the flower stems against her own chest. Her eyes stay on the flower display while his face turns toward the blurred departure board above the concourse; the offered envelope hovering just short of her open palm is the shared action that contradicts their separate public attentions. Water-darkened coats of passing commuters make a soft moving band behind the pair, and the florist's metal buckets leave a clear visual opening around the transfer. Photograph from the customer side of the stall in a horizontal waist-up two-person frame, at the woman's chest height with a natural 50mm perspective. Hold her face, his reaching hand, her open receiving hand, the whole envelope and the visible gap on the same readable focus plane. The chrysanthemums lead the eye down to the suspended offer, then back to her watchful face. Cool diffuse daylight from the concourse glazing and a restrained warm bulb above the flowers make the skin, crumpled wrapping and wet floor feel tangible, with modest film grain and ordinary photographic realism.
